text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thank you for getting in touch, C. I'm sorry about your dad. I'll act as facilitator for you, A and B, and I'll keep one running list of concerns so all three of you can see where things stand.

Here is the list as it stands now:

1. C will not sign off on A buying the house with her husband at a family discount.

I'm writing to A and B today to hear their concerns. Once they reply I'll add their points and show you the updated list. I can't give legal advice or move any money, but I can help the three of you find a plan that addresses everyone's concerns. To get started, could you tell me what you most want out of this, for example a fair share of the house's value, or time to think before any sale?
I want a fair financial share of the house’s value. I haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase, and I’m not in a rush to settle it.

Here is the list as it stands now:

1. C will not sign off on A buying the house with her husband at a family discount.
2. C wants a fair financial share of the house's value and is not in a rush to settle.

I'd like to hear your side. Could you tell me what you want from the house and why, and whether you are open to options other than buying it at a lower price? I can't give legal advice or move money, but I can help the three of you build a plan that addresses everyone's concerns.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, so we can make it our home. I’m open to discussing other options, but I can’t commit without understanding the proposed value and shares. I know C hasn’t agreed.

I can't give legal advice or move money, but I can help the three of you build a plan that addresses everyone's concerns.

Thank you. I’d like my share of the house’s value to help me start a dance studio. If it’s possible to settle that sooner rather than later, that would help, though I understand the value and timing still need to be worked out.

A question for you, A: what would a fair price look like to you, and how would you and your husband pay it? That will help C and B respond to a concrete figure rather than a discount in principle. I can't set a value or move money, but a proposal the three of you can react to would move this forward.

I can’t name a fair price yet; I’d want an independent valuation and clarity on everyone’s shares first. My husband and I would need to work out financing against that figure, and I can’t promise what we could pay.

Two points stand out. C, you want a fair share and you are not in a rush. B wants her share sooner rather than later for her dance studio. Those may sit awkwardly together, so it would help to know whether you would accept B being paid her share before you are paid yours, or whether all three of you should be paid on the same timetable. B can be paid sooner; I don’t need the same timetable. But my fair share must be valued and protected, and I can’t agree to specifics before we know the proposed price and shares.

The agreed plan so far: first, ask whoever is handling your dad's will to confirm the shares and who must agree a sale. Second, get an independent valuation of the house. Third, A comes back with a proposed price and how she and her husband would pay it. Fourth, C and B respond to that proposal, with B's payment aimed at the earliest point the valuation and will allow, and C's share valued and protected. Nothing is agreed beyond those first two steps, and I can't give legal advice or move money. Please reply if you think this misses any concern.
